comparison: Both address the taxonomic revision and naming of a new genus (C7, C35, C61, C62). OpenEval finds the taxonomic conclusion SUPPORTED based on phylogenetic and morphological evidence. Peer reviewers find it UNCERTAIN, questioning whether phylogenetic placement alone justifies naming a new genus without comparative evidence from other genus pairs in the order.

Both discuss phylogenetic placement outside Equus (C6, C59) and taxonomic implications. OpenEval evaluates the taxonomic action as SUPPORTED by multiple lines of evidence. Peer reviewers praise the phylogenomic analysis but question (UNCERTAIN) whether the evidence justifies genus-level distinction, requesting comparative phylogenetic divergence data.

Both address divergence time estimates (C34, C50-C56). OpenEval finds the estimates SUPPORTED with overlapping results from different genomic compartments. Peer reviewers find them UNCERTAIN, noting the molecular estimates are much older than the fossil record suggests and requesting fuller consideration of potential inaccuracies in molecular clock estimates.

Both discuss the discordance between molecular and fossil evidence (C103-C107, C117). OpenEval rates the evolutionary model as UNCERTAIN, noting it is speculative without direct testing. Peer reviewers also find it UNCERTAIN, stating the existing discussion is insufficient and requesting more thorough consideration of potential methodological issues with molecular clock analyses.

Both address radiocarbon dating and revised extinction chronology (C38, C78, C119, C120). OpenEval finds the dating evidence SUPPORTED with robust support from multiple laboratories. Peer reviewers also find it SUPPORTED, raising no concerns about the radiocarbon results or revised chronology.

Both address the single-species conclusion and taxonomic assignment (C5, C36, C37, C88, C93, C101). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED based on phylogenetic, morphometric, and molecular evidence. Peer reviewers also find it SUPPORTED, stating the taxonomic revision is convincing with no concerns raised about single-species status.

Both address morphometric analyses (C71, C83, C84, C86, C87). OpenEval finds the morphometric evidence SUPPORTED with strong quantitative support for morphological distinction. Peer reviewers also find it SUPPORTED, raising no concerns about the morphometric analyses supporting single-species status.

Both address nuclear genomic evidence for phylogenetic placement (C45, C46, C47, C49). OpenEval finds the nuclear genomic data SUPPORTED as part of converging evidence from independent datasets. Peer reviewers also find it SUPPORTED, praising the thoroughness of the phylogenomic analysis without challenging the nuclear genomic evidence itself.

Both address the conclusion that morphological similarity was misleading (C131, C110). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED that morphology led to incorrect phylogenetic inference. Peer reviewers also find it SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting that phylogenomic data convincingly overturned morphology-based placement despite hemionine similarities.
